Looking at this PKGBUILD file, I need to analyze only the global/top-level scope since `makepkg --printsrcinfo` sources the PKGBUILD without running any functions.

- No command substitution operators like `$(...)` or backticks executing shell commands

- No network operations (curl, wget, etc.)
- No file system operations (touch, rm, mv, etc.) in global scope
- No `eval`, `exec`, or other dangerous commands
- No base64 decoding or obfuscation

All functions (`build()`, `check()`, `package()`) are defined but not executed during `makepkg --printsrcinfo`, so their contents are out of scope for this specific safety gate.

The source URLs follow standard AUR practice of using variable substitution within quoted bash strings, which is safe and does not execute commands.

The checksums are present (not skipped), which is a good security practice.

**Conclusion:** Running `makepkg --printsrcinfo` on this PKGBUILD would only source safe variable definitions at the top level. No malicious code would execute.
